family.description: Members of this family belong to a large family of nucleotidyltransferases [[cite:PUB00005745]]. This family includes kanamycin nucleotidyltransferase (KNTase) which is a plasmid-coded enzyme responsible for some types of bacterial resistance to aminoglycosides. KNTase in-activates antibiotics by catalysing the addition of a nucleotidyl group onto the drug.
family.name: Nucleotidyltransferase domain

causal_graphs.context: Purified proteins; native-PAGE GlnB modification endpoint at 30 C after 60 min, 60 uM GlnB, UTP initiated by 1 ul of 50 mM stock into a 50 ul reaction, 1 mM ATP, 10 mM alpha-KG, 25 mM MgCl2 with or without 1 mM MnCl2. Figure 5 enzyme-free control and plotted enzyme concentrations 0.025-2 uM.

evidence.explanation: Methods and Figure 5A/B; inspected original plots, control and concentration series.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: The full-length enzyme reaction increases GlnB modification above the no-GlnD control under both tested cofactor protocols. This directly assayed biochemical conversion does not resolve individual catalytic intermediates.
edges.subject: wt-reaction

evidence.explanation: Figure 3 construct boundary and Figure 5A/B GlnD-N series; no extrapolation to the minimal domain.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: The 1-371 enzyme fragment produces GlnB modification above the no-GlnD control in both protocols, with lower effectiveness than full-length in Mg alone. Activity is not assigned to an isolated 60-aa Pfam match.
edges.subject: n-fragment-reaction

evidence.explanation: Figure 3 deltaNT boundary; Figure 5A/B deltaNT versus full-length at matched concentrations. Figure 4B retains Mn-supported removal in deltaNT.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: Replacing full-length enzyme with 329-890 deltaNT lowers the endpoint toward background under both protocols. Loss is specific to this large truncation; it does not by itself distinguish folding and catalytic contributions.
edges.subject: delta-nt

evidence.explanation: Figures 3 and 5A/B G93L; Figure 4B retains removal activity, but no global folding equivalence was demonstrated.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: The G93L enzyme gives lower GlnB modification than full-length under both protocols. Residue importance is observed; its particular catalytic or structural role remains unresolved.
edges.subject: g93l

evidence.explanation: Figures 3 and 5A/B G93V; Figure 4B retains removal activity. No precise bar-based ratio is reported.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: The G93V enzyme gives lower GlnB modification than full-length under both protocols. This assay-specific substitution effect is not proof of a universal glycine requirement in every family member.
edges.subject: g93v

evidence.explanation: Figures 3 and 5A/B distinguish G94D from G94L; Figure 4B retains removal activity.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: The G94D enzyme gives lower GlnB modification than full-length under both protocols. G94L is a contrasting retained-activity variant and is not pooled with G94D.
edges.subject: g94d

causal_graphs.family_mapping: E. coli K-12 GlnD P27249 sequence version 2, b0167/JW0162, 890 aa; PF01909 at 85-144 includes G93/G94/D107. The paper draws NT at 74-169. The 1-371 fragment contains additional sequence and domain context; deltaNT retains 329-890. Reference numbering agrees, without independent historical clone sequencing.
causal_graphs.limitations: Readout is average modified subunits per GlnB trimer, not initial velocity or an atomic chemical step. Net transfer/removal competition can affect the endpoint. G94L retains substantial activity, so loss is not universal for glycine substitutions. No precise bar-derived effect sizes, equal-folding controls or isolated 85-144 sufficiency are claimed. NTase membership does not transfer this substrate or mechanism across PF01909.

causal_graphs.context: Figure 4 native-PAGE endpoint after 60 min at 30 C, 40 uM fully modified GlnB, 0.1/0.5/2 uM GlnD, no UTP. Mg-UR uses 50 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM ATP, 0.5 mM alpha-KG and 2.5 mM glutamine. Mn-UR uses 1 mM MnCl2 and 10 mM glutamine, omitting MgCl2, ATP and alpha-KG.

evidence.explanation: Figures 3 and 4A/B HD-AA; Figure 5A/B confirms retained transfer activity. Remaining modification near background-control values means little removal.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: HD-AA reduces removal relative to full-length in both separately tested UR protocols. The effect is outside PF01909 and is retained as a biochemical domain-separation control.
edges.subject: hd-aa

evidence.explanation: Figures 3 and 4A/B HD-QN; Figure 5A/B supplies the complementary transfer assay.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: HD-QN reduces removal relative to full-length in both separately tested UR protocols while retaining transfer activity. This supports distinct functional regions without defining the atomic removal mechanism.
edges.subject: hd-qn

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P27249 sequence version 2 carries PF01909 at 85-144, but H514/D515 lie in PF01966 at 468-601. These whole-protein controls distinguish activities and do not assign demodification to PF01909.
causal_graphs.limitations: Figure 4 plots remaining UMP on an inverted axis; the encoded outcome is extent of removal, not the plotted ordinate or an initial rate. Protocols differ in several components, so comparisons are within each protocol. Figure 5 retained transfer activity argues against completely inactive preparations but does not exclude local structural changes. No metal-binding geometry is established.

causal_graphs.title: GlnD HD substitutions reduce GlnB demodification outside the PF01909 domain

causal_graphs.context: Figure 8A; Mg-only UTase protocol with GlnB, UTP, ATP and alpha-KG, 30 C/60 min endpoint. Every edge compares glutamine addition within the same enzyme construct and cofactor condition.

evidence.explanation: Figure 8A full-length paired bars; Methods define buffer and endpoint. Figure 8B is a separate condition.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: Glutamine lowers the full-length enzyme modification endpoint relative to its matched Mg-only, no-glutamine reaction. This does not directly establish glutamine binding to the NT domain.
edges.subject: glutamine-wt

evidence.explanation: Figure 8A HD-AA paired bars and Figure 4 removal control; Figure 8B lacks a comparable HD-AA response.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: Glutamine lowers the HD-AA enzyme modification endpoint in Mg-only conditions despite its loss of removal activity in Figure 4. The result supports inhibition of transfer without specifying a molecular binding relay.
edges.subject: glutamine-hd-aa

evidence.explanation: Figure 8A HD-QN paired bars and Figure 4 removal control; Figure 8B is not evidence for the same inhibitory edge.
evidence.snippet: GlnD-N showed substantial UTase activity in both conditions

edges.mechanism: Glutamine lowers the HD-QN enzyme modification endpoint in Mg-only conditions despite its loss of removal activity in Figure 4. The result is scoped to the assay and does not establish physiological metal occupancy.
edges.subject: glutamine-hd-qn

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Full-length P27249 sequence version 2 includes PF01909 at 85-144 and HD region 468-601. HD-AA/QN alter residues 514/515 outside PF01909; glutamine response is a whole-enzyme property, not a demonstrated ligand-binding function of PF01909.
causal_graphs.limitations: HD variants lack detectable UR in the separate Figure 4 assays, helping distinguish inhibited transfer from enhanced removal. Exact binding site and allosteric relay were not measured. The 1-371 fragment lacks the same inhibition, but its altered structure remains an alternative. Figure 8B Mg/Mn results differ and must not be merged into this graph; its WT endpoint can fall through competing removal.

evidence.explanation: P05057 currently returns PF07827 at 114-243 but no PF01909. ANT(4') WT/T130K/D80Y chemistry was not imported into this graph.
MntA/HepT adenylylation needs exact species and domain mapping before transfer to PF01909 members.

discussions.notes: Preserve frozen metadata. Investigate CCA, OAS, DNA nucleotidylation, CdnE, AadA/ANT9, MntA and Hailong branches separately; review their primary constructs rather than importing database summaries. Most of 24660 frozen proteins remain unassessed.
discussions.prompt: Resolve the KNTase mapping boundary and extend distinct PF01909 functional branches.
discussions.rationale: A family description and related fold are not exact protein-to-Pfam evidence, and GlnD is only one branch of this large family.

evidence.explanation: Figures 3/4/5/8 distinguish truncations, substitutions, transfer/removal and Mg-only versus Mg/Mn conditions. G94L and 1-371 glutamine response are explicit exceptions.
R. rubrum regulation differs and needs its own mapped graph; 2010 nitrogenase phenotypes are not direct E. coli chemistry.

discussions.notes: Recover raw gels, replication/uncertainty, historical clone sequence and folding controls. Expand D107 and other constructs with figure-label checks; test molecular ligand binding and catalytic intermediates separately. Main 2010 text and figures do not establish a physiological futile cycle or all-member mechanism. Keep IN_PROGRESS and retain successor review for additions.
discussions.prompt: Extend GlnD evidence while preserving domain, species and endpoint boundaries.
discussions.rationale: NT-containing fragment sufficiency is not isolated-Pfam-domain sufficiency; HD removal and glutamine regulation cannot all be assigned to the NT domain.
